entries.title: Hormuz talks positive, Oman says, as Iran warns deal would not open strait
entries.snippet: Both sides suggest progress in talks to agree a new shipping route through the strait, but a breakthrough remains unclear.

entries.title: Trump's ex-lawyer Todd Blanche narrowly confirmed as US attorney general
entries.snippet: The vote cements Trump's former criminal defence lawyer as the nation's top law enforcement official despite a rare pushback from some Republicans.

entries.title: US offers $1bn to Colombia on new right-wing president's first day of office
entries.snippet: Abelardo de la Espriella used his maiden speech to promise an "all-out war" on what he calls "narco-terrorism".

entries.title: Messi's father Jorge dies aged 68 after illness
entries.snippet: Lionel Messi's father and agent Jorge dies at the age of 68 following a long illness.

entries.title: Madonna pays tribute to 'genius, otherworldly' producer William Orbit
entries.snippet: The Queen of Pop worked with Orbit several times over the years, most notably on her genre-bending, Grammy Award-winning album Ray of Light.

entries.title: Watch: Moment opposition MP throws eggs at Kosovo's acting PM
entries.snippet: Lawmakers and police officers had to intervene after Alliance party MP Time Kadrijaj hurled at least four eggs towards Kosovo's acting prime minister Albin Kurti.

entries.title: Paris tells e-scooter riders to wear safety gear or face fines
entries.snippet: Police in the French capital tighten rules for riders after a sharp increase in fatal accidents.

entries.title: Spain imposes border controls against Italy as row over Ceuta migrant influx intensifies
entries.snippet: Italy introduced border controls following an influx of about 78,000 migrants from Morocco into the neighbouring Spanish exclave of Ceuta.

entries.title: Child among three killed in Russian missile attacks near Kyiv
entries.snippet: Russia continued its overnight attacks after President Volodymyr Zelensky warned of Ukraine's dwindling supplies of missile interceptors.

entries.title: Typhoon Dolphin batters Japan's Okinawa before bearing down on China
entries.snippet: The storm has cut power to at least 44,000 buildings and injured five people on the Japanese island.

entries.title: Fast-moving Canada wildfire doubles in size forcing thousands to flee homes
entries.snippet: The Bald Range wildfire in British Columbia, still considered "out of control", has spread to more than 36 sq miles (95 sq km).

entries.title: Thai PM vows to introduce stricter gun laws after eight killed in shooting
entries.snippet: Eight people were killed when a 14-year-old opened fire at his home and school before shooting himself dead.

entries.snippet: Pakistan says an attack on any of the three will amount to an attack against all, amid conflict in the Middle East.

entries.title: Spanish police arrest 78 people in bust of 'one of largest' smuggling networks
entries.snippet: The group moved synthetic drugs from Spain to Algeria, then used the return journey to smuggle migrants and weapons.

entries.title: NBA forward Clarke's death due to effects of drugs
entries.snippet: Memphis Grizzlies forward Brandon Clarke's death was due to the effects of heroin and cocaine, the Los Angeles medical authority reveals.

entries.title: Hunter Biden tells BBC his pardon was 'not good' for US or his father's legacy
entries.snippet: In a wide-ranging BBC interview, the former president's son denies any interest in running for office and says his father's cancer has spread.

entries.title: Book hidden in fireplace returned to Australian library 150 years overdue

entries.title: Kidnapped rare Serbian eagle freed into wild after rescue
entries.snippet: Feliks the eagle was abducted as he first flew the nest in Serbia and wound up in the Middle East with poachers who demanded a ransom.

entries.title: Australia is the planet's extinction hotspot, but one animal offers a glimmer of hope
entries.snippet: The country is home to some of the world's most unique species - but it is losing them at an alarming rate.

entries.title: The phone book that led us to Assad's spy chief in hiding

entries.title: Solar eclipse to occur next week. Here is what to know

entries.title: Tanker sailors still face danger in the Strait of Hormuz
entries.snippet: An agreement over the Strait of Hormuz is still far away. Tim Wilkins, who works for a tanker industry group, says the ships stuck around the waterway are in limbo, and transiting is still dangerous.

entries.title: Ukraine mourns 'collector of souls' Oleksiy Yukov, killed recovering war dead
entries.snippet: Oleksiy Yukov spent two decades recovering the bodies of soldiers — including many Russians. He was killed during a recovery mission after stepping on a landmine.

entries.title: K-pop's global wave inspires Chile's next pop stars
entries.snippet: K-pop conquered the world — now Chile's young creatives are remixing the movement and making it their own.

entries.title: Opinion: Europe's summer of heat
entries.snippet: Europe is in another brutal heat wave. The summer's earlier record-breaking weather already damaged crops, sparked wildfires and led to increased deaths.

entries.title: Switzerland is a neutral nation but has more nuclear bunkers than any country in the world
entries.snippet: Instead of scrapping its network of bomb shelters after the Cold War, Switzerland kept building them. The country has more than 370,000 nuclear bomb shelters. Some are now used to house migrants.

entries.title: The Women's Professional Baseball League makes its historic debut
entries.snippet: The Los Angeles Queens, the New York Heights, the Boston Hunters and the San Francisco Firebells take the field in Springfield, Ill., as the Women's Pro Baseball League kicks off its inaugural season.

entries.title: Federal funds can't be used to give test strips to drug users, raising overdose fears
entries.snippet: Drug addiction groups are reeling after Trump officials said federal grants cannot be used to hand out test strips to drug users. The strips help users check street drugs for dangerous adulterants.

entries.title: Private prisons announce $1.4 billion in revenue as immigration detentions climb
entries.snippet: That revenue does not include net proceeds of $1.6 billion made by CoreCivic after the recent sale of four of their facilities to the Department of Homeland Security.

entries.title: Data centers are a political issue crossing party lines, driving voters to candidates
entries.snippet: Wisconsin Democratic candidate for governor Francesca Hong called for a moratorium on data centers. So did Ohio Republican governor hopeful Vivek Ramaswamy, as data centers begin to dominate campaigns.

entries.title: Wildfires force 20,000 to flee as British Columbia declares state of emergency
entries.snippet: Premier David Eby announced the emergency as more than 100 wildfires burned across the province, nearly half of them out of control in hot, windy weather and prolonged drought.

entries.title: ICE says it expects to equip every field officer with body cameras by the end of August
entries.snippet: The agency defended its body-worn camera policy amid questions about provisions allowing ICE leadership to withhold or indefinitely delay footage after serious injuries or deaths in custody.

entries.title: How Troy Jackson went from Maine logger to Democratic nominee for Senate against Susan Collins
entries.snippet: Jackson's campaign has focused on his ties to Aroostook County, a sprawling, wooded region known as "The County" to Mainers.

entries.title: A New Mexico judge ordered new child safeguards for Meta. Advocates hope other courts follow
entries.snippet: The judge's order showed a possible path forward for other court fights around the country as Meta faces mounting legal, regulatory and public pressure to do more to protect young people.

entries.title: What are Zyn nicotine pouches and are they safe?
entries.snippet: The Food and Drug Administration is allowing the company Zyn to advertise some of its nicotine pouches as safer in some ways than smoking cigarettes.

entries.title: 12-year-old girl dies after Thailand school shooting, bringing death toll to at least 8
entries.snippet: A 14-year-old opened fire at around 10 a.m. Friday at Debsirin Nonthaburi School in Nonthaburi province northwest of the Thai capital before apparently taking his own life.

entries.title: Lake Mead hits historic low water level as Colorado River struggles
entries.snippet: The record follows a winter that produced the worst snowpack on record in the Colorado River Basin.

entries.title: What to know about Trump's new attempt to limit birthright citizenship
entries.snippet: A Supreme Court decision in June struck down a previous attempt at restricting birthright citizenship, but Thursday's orders were made with "adjustments" keeping the decision in mind, President Donald Trump said.

entries.title: Todd Blanche narrowly confirmed as Trump's attorney general in overnight vote
entries.snippet: The Republican-led Senate voted 50-49 to make Blanche the second confirmed attorney general since Trump returned to the White House last year with a stated desire to use the law enforcement agency to investigate his political enemies.

entries.title: Advocates for former U.S. Marine held for years in Russia say he is near death
entries.snippet: A former U.S. Marine held in Russia for more than four years on disputed charges is gravely ill and at risk of dying, his family and advocates said Friday.

entries.title: ICE will only release body camera video when in agency's 'best interests,' policy says
entries.snippet: Immigration and Customs Enforcement is moving to equip officers with body cameras in the next two months but the agency's policy gives it broad control over what footage will be made public by specifying any releases must be in its "best interests."

entries.title: Judge orders Virginia county to replace Confederate names it restored to schools in 2024
entries.snippet: A federal judge has sided with the Virginia NAACP in its lawsuit against a county school board's reinstatement of Confederate military names to two schools, saying the decision discriminated against Black students and ordering the board to change the schools' monikers again.

entries.title: What's holding up the Iran-Oman proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz

entries.title: Colombia's new president reflects Latin America's right-wing shift
entries.snippet: The new president of Colombia was inaugurated on Friday. Abelardo de la Espriella won a tight race in June, ending Colombia's leftist movement with a sharp pivot to the right. Liz Landers takes a look at the president and his tight relationship with the Trump White House.

entries.title: Drought and aging infrastructure plunge Puerto Rico into a water crisis

entries.title: Brooks and Capehart on what progressive primary wins mean for Democrats

entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: FIFA warns against 'concerted effort' to undermine Gianni Infantino
entries.snippet: Pressure is mounting on the FIFA president Gianni Infantino after plans to sell a stake in the World Cup collapsed and fresh allegations emerged relating to his time at UEFA.

entries.title: Germany: Interior Minister warns of 'daily' hybrid warfare
entries.snippet: German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt says attacks by foreign powers have become a constant threat to Germany. His remarks come just days after an explosive-laden drone was found at Leipzig airport.

entries.title: Nigeria marries 1,500 couples in mass wedding
entries.snippet: The government describes the program as a way to support low-income families and promote social stability. Among those married were people who lost family members in violent attacks.

entries.title: Kosovo PM Kurti egged in parliament amid political crisis
entries.snippet: Kosovo has held three elections in over two years. Albin Kurti's ruling Vetevendosje is struggling to garner the two-thirds majority required to elect a president.

entries.title: Thousands attend Prague Pride parade
entries.snippet: Participants observed a minute of silence in memory of the victims of a van ramming near the CSD parade in Berlin. The march was accompanied by enhanced security measures.

entries.title: US Senate confirms Trump loyalist Todd Blanche as new AG
entries.snippet: Republicans dropped their opposition and confirmed President Donald Trump's former defense lawyer to a Cabinet position. Now, Todd Blanche will act as the nation's top law enforcement officer.

entries.title: Ukraine: Russia pounds Kyiv as Zelenskyy visits Serbia
entries.snippet: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy is visiting Serbia, a country that has traditionally been friendly with Moscow, as Russia strikes the Kyiv region once again.

entries.title: Iran war: IRGC says Hormuz to open if US accepts Iran's terms
entries.snippet: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said the reopening of the vital Strait of Hormuz did not depend on the outcome of ongoing talks with Oman. DW has more.

entries.title: War, terror, diplomacy: What if Israel takes Al-Aqsa Mosque?
entries.snippet: Reports from Jerusalem suggest that Israeli authorities are taking over one of Islam's holiest sites, the Al-Aqsa Mosque. If they do, experts say anything could happen, from war to terrorism to ending diplomatic ties.

entries.title: Bulgaria: Unknown drone explodes near Romanian border
entries.snippet: A drone that entered Bulgaria's airspace exploded near the Romanian border and the Trans-Balkan gas pipeline, the Bulgarian prime minister said. Bulgaria summoned the Ukrainian ambassador for consultations.

entries.title: EU holds talks with big tech over Ceuta misinformation
entries.snippet: EU digital chief Henna Virkkunen has called for closer monitoring of social media platforms moving forward, amid the spread of misinformation during the recent migrant influx at Spain's Ceuta.

entries.title: When German Catholics and Protestants share a church
entries.snippet: Each year, dozens of churches are decommissioned, demolished or repurposed in Germany. But there is a new, unique development.

entries.title: Germany news: Trucking rules eased as rivers run low
entries.snippet: Several states will let trucks use motorways on Sundays and holidays as freight shipping is hampered by low water levels. The body of a German sailor missing for days has been found in the southern Aegean. DW has more.

entries.title: India wary of potential 100% US tariffs over Russian oil
entries.snippet: The US Senate passed a sanctions bill that could result in tariffs on India as a major consumer of Russian oil.

entries.title: Typhoon Dolphin hits Japan as China braces for coming storm
entries.snippet: A typhoon is lashing Japan's south, causing injuries and blackouts. It is now headed for China, where ports have been closed in preparation.

entries.title: Germany debates reintroducing mandatory civilian service
entries.snippet: Social organizations are skeptical about the government's ideas for a civilian service program that youths could choose as an alternative should Germany reinstate mandatory military conscription.

entries.title: Ceuta: Spain sets up border controls on travelers from Italy
entries.snippet: Spain had warned Italy it would impose entry checks on visitors unless Rome halts its controls by Sunday. Even though they don't share a land border, the countries entered a spat after the Ceuta border rush.

entries.title: Colombia: Trump ally De la Espriella takes office
entries.snippet: Conservative Abelardo de la Espriella was sworn in as Colombia's president, promising to crack down on armed drug gangs.

entries.title: Iceland’s EU vote: A nation divided over Europe
entries.snippet: Security concerns, control over fishing rights and rising living costs are shaping Iceland's debate over whether to restart talks on joining the European Union.
